sample_unit: CT examinations (30,678 CTPA and 37,191 routine contrast-enhanced CTs)

links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of FDA-cleared PE AI on local historical data versus clearance benchmarks
links.effect: PE model 86.8% sensitivity, 99.1% specificity; iPE model 73.5% sensitivity, 99.8% specificity. Sensitivity was lower than FDA-clearance benchmarks while specificity exceeded them.
links.quote: Both models demonstrated lower sensitivity than FDA-clearance benchmarks while exceeding cleared specificity, with diminishing performance for peripheral and non-acute emboli mirroring known human reader limitations and underscoring the need for standardized post-market surveillance of AI-enabled medical devices.

links.outcome: AI performance across a 17-facility health system
links.effect: Evaluated across 17 facilities, but the abstract reports only pooled performance, not per-site results.
links.quote: We retrospectively evaluated two FDA-cleared AI algorithms from a single commercial platform (Aidoc Medical BriefCase), one for PE triage on dedicated CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA; n = 30,678) and one for incidental PE (iPE) detection on routine contrast-enhanced CTs (n = 37,191), across a 17-facility academic health system.

screen.reason: Retrospective multi-site evaluation of commercial FDA-cleared AI algorithms for PE and incidental PE detection using a local health system dataset and LLM label extraction, demonstrating the need for post-market surveillance but not testing a specific deployment safeguard intervention.
